title: Hormuz disruption threatens Europe’s economic recovery: KPMG
summary:
KPMG UK has warned that disruption to the Strait of Hormuz is triggering a renewed energy and supply chain shock across Europe, raising inflation and slowing growth. 
UK GDP growth is forecast to slow to 0.8 per cent in 2026, while Eurozone inflation is projected at 3.1 per cent. 
Higher energy, transport and commodity costs may pressure industries.

title: ITCPE Guangzhou 2026 sets new records in global participation
summary:
The 21st ITCPE Guangzhou concluded successfully with nearly 40,000 professional visitors and around 800 exhibitors across 50,000 square metres.
Overseas buyer registrations jumped 92.97 per cent YoY, while on-site transactions rose 42 per cent.
The expo highlighted digital printing, intelligent sewing, eco-friendly dyeing and seamless textile technologies.

title: Germany’s Mayer & Cie Global will showcase new vision at ITM 2026
summary:
Mayer & Cie. Global will showcase its renewed business direction at ITM 2026 in Istanbul alongside partner Mayer Mümessillik.
The company will present two OV 3.2 QCe circular knitting machines while highlighting its transition from a machinery maker to a solution-focused premium brand, combining German engineering expertise with greater agility and customer focus.

title: Russia clears Indonesia–EAEU FTA for implementation to expand trade
summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin recently signed a law that ratifies an FTA between the Eurasian Economic Union and Indonesia. 
The FTA ensures preferential terms for nearly 90 per cent of commodities and grants the most favoured regime status for goods from both sides with exceptions. 
Agricultural and manufactured goods from Indonesia will gain wider market access, boosting regional supply chains.

title: Laos seeks Vietnam support to boost logistics infra, transport routes
summary:
To transform Laos from a landlocked country into a regional connectivity hub linking the Mekong sub-region and the ASEAN, the country is implementing its Trade and Transport Facilitation Action Plan for 2025-2030, according to a senior Laotian official. 
The country is also seeking Vietnam’s support in sharing experience and enhancing logistics infrastructure and transport routes.

title: India’s cotton stock to rise sharply to 85 lakh bales in 2025-26: CAI
summary:
India’s cotton closing stocks for the 2025-26 season are projected to rise sharply to 85.59 lakh bales due to weak export demand and higher imports, according to CAI.
Cotton imports are estimated at 47 lakh bales, while exports are expected to remain flat.
Higher domestic availability and increased production are likely to raise carryover stocks significantly by September 2026.

title: ICE cotton sees mixed trend amid rainfall & stronger US dollar
summary:
ICE cotton futures showed a mixed trend as favourable rainfall across US growing regions and a stronger dollar pressured nearby contracts, while higher crude oil prices supported deferred months.
Improved planting progress and rising certified stocks added bearish sentiment.
However, geopolitical tensions and concerns over future acreage and weather risks continued to support longer-dated contracts.

title: Iran war fuels energy uncertainty for UK businesses: BCC survey
summary:
A British Chambers of Commerce survey found 80 per cent of UK firms are experiencing or expecting disruption from the Iran conflict, mainly through higher energy prices, shipping delays and rising raw material costs. 
Manufacturing reported the biggest impact. 
Around 75 per cent of businesses expect energy bills to rise over the next year, while more than a third anticipate difficulties paying costs.

title: German industrial sales, goods exports robust in Q1 2026: Bundesbank
summary:
The German economy is more robust than expected earlier despite burdens, the Deutsche Bundesbank said in its May report. 
Industrial sales and goods exports were robust in Q1 2026. 
Averaged over Q1 2026, industrial production was significantly weaker than in Q4 2025. 
The labour market was unable to gain from fairly strong Q1 2026 economic growth, and inflation may remain higher over the coming months.

title: Dedicated India-China ocean service to be launched on June 4
summary:
Danish integrated logistics company Maersk recently announced the launch of FI2, a dedicated ocean service connecting Far East Asia to the Indian subcontinent, with the first Westbound sailing departing Shanghai on June 4.
The service will provide Indian businesses with a quicker, reliable, high-frequency connection to key manufacturing and sourcing hubs across North West India, Maersk said.

title: Price check: What 38% of Europeans want from green fashion
summary:
European consumers increasingly expect brands and governments to make sustainable fashion more affordable, transparent and accessible.
Regulations such as DPP and Extended Producer Responsibility EPR are pushing companies towards greater accountability.
However, high prices, greenwashing concerns and limited consumer awareness continue to slow wider adoption of sustainable fashion.

title: Japan’s apparel imports rebound to $2.1 bn in April 2026
summary:
Japan’s apparel imports rebounded in April 2026 after declining in March, reaching around $2.17 billion and accounting for 3.4 per cent of total imports.
Textile yarn and fabric imports and exports also posted gains, while textile machinery exports rose strongly.
Over recent fiscal years, Japan has maintained relatively steady growth in apparel imports and machinery exports.

title: India’s Sahu International Attire to build RMG unit in UP’s YEIDA belt
summary:
Sahu International Attire will invest ₹700 million in a garment manufacturing facility in the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority region of Uttar Pradesh (UP) state that is expected to create 2,000 jobs. 
The company is among 17 firms that received allotment letters by UP chief minister Yogi Adityanath for setting up projects covering several sectors, including solar energy and green energy.

title: Hong Kong apparel imports edge down in Q1 2026
summary:
Hong Kong’s apparel imports declined slightly to $1.431 billion in January-March 2026 amid softer sourcing activity.
China remained the largest supplier despite a marginal fall in market share, while Vietnam, France and Japan expanded their presence.
The trading hub continued to maintain its role as an independent customs territory and global re-export centre.

title: Coats & JACK launch integrated solution for Chinese apparel SMEs
summary:
Coats Group PLC & JACK Technology Co Ltd have signed a strategic cooperation agreement to accelerate innovation for China’s growing apparel SME sector. 
The partnership combines Coats’ high-performance thread, digital software and technical support with JACK’s intelligent sewing equipment to help manufacturers improve shop-floor efficiency, productivity and inventory management.

title: Sri Lanka apparel exports decline amid weaker global demand: JAAF
summary:
Sri Lanka’s apparel exports fell 4.72 per cent year-on-year to $328.15 million in April 2026 due to weaker demand from the UK, EU, and US markets, according to JAAF.
Exports to other destinations rose 12.61 per cent, highlighting diversification opportunities.
JAAF said improving competitiveness and policy support will be crucial for long-term sector growth.

title: US’ Deckers sees continued growth momentum for HOKA and UGG in FY26
summary:
Deckers Brands has reported record FY26 revenue of $5.47 billion, up 9.8 per cent YoY, with diluted EPS rising 11 per cent to $7.02, driven by strong HOKA and UGG sales. 
Fourth-quarter revenue increased 9.6 per cent to $1.12 billion. 
The company forecast high-single-digit sales growth for FY27 and expanded its share repurchase authorisation to approximately $5 billion.

title: New Zealand’s apparel imports dips 8% to $88 mn in April 2026
summary:
New Zealand’s apparel imports fell 8 per cent year on year to NZ$150.50 million in April 2026, reflecting a softer start to fiscal 2026–27, with sharper weakness in non-knitted garments.
In contrast, apparel exports rose 19.3 per cent, led by strong growth in knitted apparel.
Fabric imports increased, indicating resilient demand for textile inputs despite weaker garment sourcing.

title: Argentina’s apparel imports rise 68% in Q1; China retains edge
summary:
Argentina’s apparel imports surged 68 per cent year on year to $238.84 million in Q1 2026, reflecting stronger domestic demand and faster sourcing activity. 
China retained its lead, accounting for 56.7 per cent of import value and 77.1 per cent of volume, while Vietnam, Bangladesh and Cambodia also posted strong gains, highlighting broad-based growth in Argentina’s apparel imports.

title: Crochet, linen & ballet: The styles ruling Spring/Summer 2026
summary:
Spring/Summer 2026 fashion is led by breathable, comfort-driven styles such as crochet, linen, knitted sets, flowy trousers, and tailored shirts. 
Experts highlight ‘controlled ease,' blending relaxed silhouettes with sharper details. 
Ballet-inspired dressing, napkin tops, artisan knits and maximalist prints are gaining traction, while Gen Z is moving away from rigid seasons towards more fluid.
